title: This Week, Last Week, Next Week

sections.title: hét: both "seven" and "week"
sections.content: hét is a word you already know as the number "seven" — it's also the ordinary word for "week". Context always makes it clear which one is meant. To talk about WHICH week, put a small word in front: ezen a héten (this week), múlt héten (last week), jövő héten (next week).

items.english: This week I'm working a lot.
Next week I have Hungarian class on Tuesday.

sections.content: múlt literally means "past" and jövő means "future" — they're ordinary adjectives, not a special grammatical form, so once you know them you can reuse them elsewhere: a múlt (the past), a jövő (the future).
